text: DSH Always-On 是面向容器或远程主机部署的 DSH 网页端插件：它在文件卡片、变更文件和侧边栏预览中提供下载入口，并可从会话页头打开文件侧栏。用户可在侧边栏编辑文本文件并保存回 Harness 主机；编辑器支持 Monaco，也会在 CDN 不可用时回退到纯文本模式。保存会检查文件版本并遵循会话沙箱策略，未保存修改会提示确认。适合通过浏览器管理远程 DSH 工作区文件的用户。首次使用编辑器需要浏览器能访问 cdn.jsdelivr.net；不需要额外 API 密钥。

DSH Always-On adds downloads, a Files shortcut, and a text editor for remote DSH workspaces. Save edits to the Harness host with version checks and its sandbox policy. Monaco loads from jsDelivr with a plain text fallback; browser access to cdn.jsdelivr.net is needed. No API key is required.
我在浏览器里用远程 DSH，怎么把生成的文件下载到本机？
希望直接从会话页面打开工作区文件列表。
容器里的 DSH 不能访问我的电脑文件，能在网页侧边栏查看和修改文本吗？
文件保存时如果远程磁盘内容已经变化，怎样避免直接覆盖？
Can I download files produced by a DSH session running on a server?
I want to edit a workspace text file in the browser and save it to the remote host.
DSH Always-On 的功能「下载工作区文件」：在生成文件卡片、变更文件和侧边栏文件预览处提供下载按钮，用户点击后通过 Harness 路由将单个文件流式传回浏览器。
DSH Always-On 的功能「侧栏文本编辑」：用户从文件预览按 Edit，在独立侧栏标签中编辑文本并保存；保存请求带有读取时的版本信息，遇到文件变更可选择重新载入、覆盖或继续编辑。
DSH Always-On 的功能「打开文件侧栏」：会话页头提供 Show files 按钮，点击后打开或聚焦 Files 标签，方便从当前会话进入工作区文件浏览。
DSH Always-On 使用编辑器时会从 cdn.jsdelivr.net 加载 Monaco；该 CDN 可看到浏览器 IP 地址和 User-Agent，首次打开编辑器需要浏览器能够访问该域名。

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · @louisremi/dsh-always-on：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin for running your Harness in a container, where it has **no access to your local file system**.

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · @louisremi/dsh-always-on：Run the Harness in a Docker container — on a NAS, a server, anywhere — and it lives on a machine of its own: the stock "show file location" and "Open in app" buttons would have to reach a desktop that isn't there, and nothing inside the container can read or write your computer's files. Your browser is the only connection between you and your files. This plugin makes it enough, replacing the dead buttons with things that work through it:

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @louisremi/dsh-always-on
```

Use the name of the profile your Harness runs with. The plugin loads live; restart the Harness only if the command says a restart is required.

Installing from a git URL builds the plugin on install (`prepare` runs `npm run build`). If your profile is managed by pnpm it may block build scripts until you approve them (`allowBuilds`); a skipped build leaves the plugin without its `dist/`.

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · Usage：Nothing to configure.

**Download.** The download button appears wherever the folder button used to be: file cards under an agent reply (`present`) and in the changed-files review tab, the toolbar of a file open in the sidebar preview, and the empty state of a file the preview can't render.

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · Usage：**Show files.** The workspace folder button in the session header becomes a single **Show files** button. It opens (or focuses) the sidebar's Files tab. Inside that tab the button is hidden, since it would do nothing.

**Edit.** Open a text file in the sidebar preview and press **Edit** (pencil icon, next to Download). The file opens in its own editor tab:

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · Usage：- `Ctrl/Cmd+S` or the **Save** button writes the file; a dot on the tab and filename marks unsaved changes.
- If the file changed on disk after you opened it, saving is refused and you choose **Reload from disk**, **Overwrite**, or **Keep editing**. Nothing is overwritten silently.
- Closing a tab (or the browser page) with unsaved changes asks for confirmation.
- Line endings (LF/CRLF) and a leading UTF-8 byte-order mark are preserved.
- Text files up to 1 MiB. Binary files and invalid UTF-8 are refused, not corrupted.
- Saving follows the session's sandbox mode: it fails in read-only mode and outside the workspace in workspace-write mode, exactly like the agent's own file tools.

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · How it works：The plugin adds two authenticated routes to the Harness, `GET /api/download.file` and `POST /api/save.file`, and registers its buttons in the same UI slots as the stock ones, shadowing them (disable the plugin and the stock buttons return). "Show files" calls the sidebar's public `openTab('files')`; the editor is a sidebar tab type registered through the public sidebar API. Downloads stream straight to disk, so large files are fine. Saves go through the Harness's own filesystem layer with the session's sandbox policy and a version check.

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · The editor and the CDN：To keep the package small (~69 kB), Monaco is **not bundled**. On the first Edit it is loaded from [jsDelivr](https://www.jsdelivr.com/) at a pinned version (`monaco-editor@0.52.2`).

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · The editor and the CDN：- It runs in a **sandboxed iframe** (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`, no `allow-same-origin`) with a Content-Security-Policy that only permits the CDN. The CDN's code therefore cannot read the Harness page, your session cookie, local storage, or call the Harness API; it only exchanges messages with the editor wrapper.
- The loader script is checked with Subresource Integrity (SRI). Files the loader then pulls in are not individually pinned by hash, which is why the isolation above matters.
- **Your browser needs internet access to `cdn.jsdelivr.net`** (the Harness host does not). If it is unreachable or blocked, the editor falls back to a plain `<textarea>` with the same save, conflict and dirty-state behaviour, and says so.
- jsDelivr sees your IP address and user agent when Monaco loads.

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · Development：The source is TypeScript; `npm run build` compiles it to `dist/` (it also runs automatically via `prepare` on install and pack). The tests run `.ts` files directly through Node's native type stripping, so **developing** needs Node ≥ 22.18 (or ≥ 23.6) — the plugin itself still only requires Node ≥ 20 at runtime.

```sh
npm ci
npm run check      # TypeScript typecheck of src, tests and e2e
npm run build      # compile src/ to dist/
npm test           # host route unit tests (no browser needed)
@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · Development：`test:e2e` needs Chromium, `playwright-core` and React 18 UMD builds; see the header of `e2e/browser.e2e.mts`.

@louisremi/dsh-always-on README · Releasing：Changes land on `main` as pull requests, so each GitHub Release can describe itself: create a release with an empty description and the **Release notes** workflow fills it from everything merged since the previous release (`.github/release.yml` controls the categorization).
